offer.say: Grandpa opened this building. Cut the ribbon, lost the opening game, came back every week anyway and shouted SKATE! from right here. He'd have been a hundred this winter. I'd like one night. Not a big thing. A SKATE! thing.

options.text: Harold Penner Night. Let's do it.
Did he ever shout anything else?

why.say: Loud at games, quiet at home. Ordered anything anybody asked for, even the things we'd never sell. Once ordered a single left skate for a man who'd lost his leg in the mill. Never told anyone. I found the invoice.

else.say: 'SKATE!' and, one time in 1983, 'THAT'S MY GRANDDAUGHTER'S TEACHER!' at a referee. It was. She failed me that year. Unrelated, she said.

options.text: Ha. Let's give him a night.

decline.say: Of course. He'd say there's no rush. Then he'd shout at you to hurry up.

accepted.say: Thank you. I'll bring a cushion for the seat. He always said the seats were too hard. He was on the committee that chose them.

options.text: I'll talk to Ray about the Kings.

p_night.say: I've told everyone at the store. The paint counter's coming. The paint counter is a very loyal crowd.

complete.say: Six hundred people and every one of them shouted it at the opening faceoff. I could hear him in it. Here. The cushion. For C-4-7. Somebody should sit there who'll shout. Now, who shouted first?

options.text: You did, June. It was always going to be you.
Irene Dubois. She said he still owed her a dance.
Stan, at the rafters end. Out of nowhere.

c_june.say: I did. I didn't know I was going to. It just came out, like it does in our family.

c_irene.say: Irene! She told me he never did dance with her. She shouted it like she was collecting. I think she was.

c_stan.say: Stan Szymanski. He's never said a word at a game in fifty years. He said SKATE! and then he leaned on the rail, very pleased with himself.

done.say: Every year, then. He'd like that. He'd shout about it.
